title: Trello Cards Not Loading: How to Fix It
body_md:
![support.atlassian.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/trello-cards-not-loading-how-to-fix-it/1.png)
*Screenshot of support.atlassian.com ([source](https://support.atlassian.com/trello/docs/troubleshooting-browser-issues-with-trello/))*

**Quick fix:** Start by checking whether a board filter hides the cards or a stale cache affects rendering. Look at the top of your board for an active filter and clear it — then, if cards are still missing, hard-refresh the page and clear your browser cache for trello.com, which is Atlassian's own first-line fix for browser issues with Trello.

## Why This Happens

![support.atlassian.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/trello-cards-not-loading-how-to-fix-it/2.png)
*Screenshot of support.atlassian.com ([source](https://support.atlassian.com/trello/docs/troubleshooting-a-slow-board/))*

Trello is a single-page web app, so "cards not loading" usually isn't a data-loss problem — it's a display or delivery problem. The usual suspects:

- **An active filter or a saved view.** If you filtered by a label, member, or due date and never cleared it, the rest of the board is still there — you just can't see it. Atlassian's browser doc even lists filters not working as one of the odd behaviors people hit after logging in.
- **Stale browser cache or blocked cookies.** Atlassian's support docs specifically call out cookies as a factor and list id.atlassian.com, auth.atlassian.com, and trello.com as the domains to check in your per-site settings.
- **Browser extensions.** Ad blockers, privacy tools, and Trello-specific extensions can intercept requests or hide cards. Atlassian's browser troubleshooting article covers extensions as a distinct step.
- **A board that's simply too big.** Trello loads open cards and attachments every time a board opens, and Atlassian suggests staying under 1,000 open cards per board — under 500 if the cards carry a lot of attachments or checklists.
- **A Trello-side incident.** Sometimes it's not you. Atlassian runs a public status page for Trello at trello.status.atlassian.com.
- **Local app data problems** on the desktop or mobile apps.

## Step-by-Step Fixes

![support.atlassian.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/trello-cards-not-loading-how-to-fix-it/3.png)
*Screenshot of support.atlassian.com ([source](https://support.atlassian.com/trello/docs/troubleshooting-for-the-desktop-app-windows-and-macos/))*

### 1. Clear any active board filter

Open the board and check the top bar. If it shows that filters are applied, open the filter menu and clear everything. This is a possible cause of "my cards disappeared," and it takes five seconds to rule out.

While you're in there, a handy trick from Atlassian's docs: open the filter menu, type an asterisk (*) in the keyword field, and every card on the board shows up with a total count at the top of the results. If the count looks right, your cards exist and this is purely a display issue.

### 2. Hard-refresh the page

Press **Ctrl + Shift + R** (Windows) or **Cmd + Shift + R** (Mac). This forces the browser to pull fresh files instead of reusing cached ones. If lists render but cards stay blank, this is a troubleshooting step worth trying.

### 3. Test in a private/incognito window

Open a private window and log into Trello. Atlassian lists a private/incognito tab as one of its standard browser checks, and it works because incognito runs without most extensions and with a clean cache. If your cards load there, the problem is local — move on to steps 4 and 5.

### 4. Clear your cache and check cookie permissions

Atlassian's browser troubleshooting guide treats clearing cache and allowing cookies as core steps. In Chrome, go to **Settings → Privacy and security → Delete browsing data**, and clear cached images and files. Then confirm cookies aren't blocked for trello.com, id.atlassian.com, and auth.atlassian.com — if a strict privacy setting blocks any of those, Trello can fail to authenticate and render an empty board.

### 5. Disable extensions one at a time

If policy permits, temporarily disable non-essential extensions and test again, then re-enable them one at a time. Do not disable a managed security extension or required VPN. Ask your IT team to help with corporate-managed browsers.

### 6. Check Trello's status page

Head to **trello.status.atlassian.com**. If there's an active incident, stop troubleshooting and wait it out. Nothing on your end will fix a server-side problem.

### 7. Fix the desktop app specifically

Atlassian's first desktop step is to close the app completely, reboot the device, and reopen the app. If that fails, the next documented step is the "Reset local data" option in the app's "Help" menu, followed by a full close and relaunch. Before you use it, confirm recent changes have reached the server — resetting local state can discard unsent changes. Atlassian also suggests checking antivirus, firewall, VPN, and proxy settings, and allowlisting Trello if one of them turns out to be the culprit, but keep managed security software enabled and let IT investigate network restrictions. See [Atlassian's desktop troubleshooting](https://support.atlassian.com/trello/docs/troubleshooting-for-the-desktop-app-windows-and-macos/).

### 8. Fix the mobile app

On Android, Atlassian's sequence is to close the app completely and reopen it first, then try clearing the cache, logging out and back in, or reinstalling the app. One important caveat: these actions clear any offline changes that haven't synced yet, so check for unsent changes before you do them.

### 9. Trim an oversized board

If a specific board is the only one that struggles, it's probably too heavy. Atlassian suggests archiving what you're not actively using: archiving a list stops it from showing every time you open the board, and you can un-archive it later or still search for those cards. If you're actively using everything, the documented alternative is to create a second board and move lists over.

### 10. Grab the console error

If nothing works, capture the error before you contact support. Atlassian's docs list the shortcuts: Chrome uses Cmd+Opt+J (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+J (Windows), Firefox uses Cmd+Opt+K or Ctrl+Shift+K, and in Safari you enable the "Develop" menu under the Advanced tab in Preferences. A screenshot of the console gets you a real answer much faster than "it doesn't work."

## How to Prevent It Next Time

![support.atlassian.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/trello-cards-not-loading-how-to-fix-it/4.png)
*Screenshot of support.atlassian.com ([source](https://support.atlassian.com/trello/docs/troubleshooting-for-the-android-app/))*

- **Archive aggressively.** Move completed lists to the archive monthly instead of letting a board balloon past a thousand cards.
- **Split giant boards.** One board per quarter or per project beats one mega-board that crawls on every load.
- **Keep trello.com whitelisted** in your ad blocker and cookie settings, especially if you use strict privacy extensions.
- **Bookmark the status page.** Checking trello.status.atlassian.com first saves you from reinstalling apps during an outage.
- **Stay on a supported, updated browser.** Updating the browser is the first item on Atlassian's own list.

*Updated October 2026: card limits, cookie domains, and the desktop "Reset local data" path re-checked against Atlassian's docs. This guide is based on that documentation, not a controlled diagnostic test.*

## My Take

My read is that most "Trello cards not loading" reports are two problems wearing one costume, and sorting them takes about a minute. Either the data isn't reaching your browser (cache, cookies, an extension, an outage) or the data is there and something is hiding it (a filter). The asterisk trick in the filter menu separates those two worlds faster than any other step, which is why I'd run it before touching cache settings.

I think the board-size guidance deserves more attention than it gets. Atlassian's own number is under 1,000 open cards, or under 500 with heavy attachments and checklists — and if your team has been dumping tasks into one board since 2023, you are the incident. Clearing cache on a 1,500-card board buys you one fast load and nothing more.

The fair counterpoint: not every slow or blank board is self-inflicted. Users do report lag on small boards after interface changes, and Atlassian has shipped desktop bugs serious enough to warrant a Jira ticket and a hardware-acceleration workaround. Checking the status page early isn't laziness, it's triage.

One caution I'd underline: "Reset local data" and mobile cache clearing are destructive to unsynced work. I'd treat those as late-stage steps, not warm-ups, especially if you've been working offline. And on managed laptops, I think the right move is to stop at step 5 and call IT — fighting a corporate security extension is not a productivity win. I'm not an IT professional, so treat any policy-level change as something to confirm with whoever owns your device.
